en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape among all Philippine volcanoes.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is a critically endangered species endemic to the tropical forests of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of approximately 2,954 meters above sea level.
Taal Volcano sits on Volcano Island within Lake Taal, making it a unique geological feature of an active volcano inside a lake.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its pristine coral atolls.
Samar is the third-largest island in the Philippines and is connected to Leyte by the San Juanico Strait.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Baguio City is called the Summer Capital of the Philippines because its high elevation provides a significantly cooler climate.
Mount Hamiguitan in Davao Oriental features a unique pygmy forest where century-old trees grow only a few meters tall.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are ancient agricultural landscapes carved into the mountains over two thousand years ago.
